title: Designing Tables
projectGoals: Entities: customers, addresses, products, categories, product_categories, inventory, carts, cart_items, orders, order_items, payments, shipments
Rules: unique SKU; non-negative prices and stock; quantity > 0; historical unit price snapshot; valid order/payment states; deliberate delete behaviour
Artifacts: ER diagram, data dictionary, migrations, seed data, 20 SQL queries, constraint tests
acceptance: Historical order totals do not change when catalogue prices change

title: Making Queries Fast
blurb: Performance optimization with plans and indexes.
projectGoals: Generate 50k–100k products with realistic category, price, status, name and timestamp distributions
Workload: SKU lookup; category + active + newest; price range; name search; category counts
Baseline with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS); add ONE index at a time; compare plans, latency, buffers and write cost
Try composite/partial B-tree, lower(name) expression index, GIN for full-text / JSONB
acceptance: Indexes rejected because they did not help

title: Transactions
projectGoals: POST /orders with idempotency key, stock validation/reservation, order + items, rollback on failure
Transaction + row locking or a carefully designed conditional UPDATE; check affected-row counts
Tests: two concurrent requests for the final unit, duplicate retries, simulated failure, payment-provider timeout (separately)
acceptance: No duplicate order for the same idempotency key

title: Scaling
projectGoals: Diagram primary + read replica + cache + backup/WAL; label read/write paths and consistency requirements
Workload assumptions: active users, req/s, read/write ratio, growth, peak, availability target
Compare in order: vertical scaling, pooling, indexing, partitioning, read replicas, sharding
Define RPO/RTO, failover, replica-lag handling, restore drills, shard key, hot-key mitigation, rebalancing

title: Django & API Engineering
blurb: The framework layer interviews probe next: ORM, APIs, background jobs and security.
projectGoals: Products, cart, checkout (POST /orders with an Idempotency-Key), order history and admin product updates
DRF with cursor pagination, ordering allowlists, object-level permissions and throttling
assertNumQueries on every list endpoint; versioned migrations including a concurrent index
Celery for post-order work using on_commit and idempotent tasks; Redis cache-aside with invalidation
manage.py check --deploy clean; CSRF and CORS configured deliberately
Docker Compose, structured logs, health checks; unit, integration, concurrency and API tests
acceptance: No N+1 on list endpoints, proved by tests
Concurrent checkout never oversells and a repeated Idempotency-Key never creates a second order
check --deploy passes and no endpoint exposes another user's data
README with setup, architecture diagram and benchmark results
